ui.note.title: A note
note.01: Day one inside the seal. The Inquisition's wall is behind me now. Whatever they're hiding, it's mine to find. — a hopeful hand
note.02: They say a man named Rosmund went deeper than anyone and came back rich as a king. They say a lot of things up there.
note.03: Three of us came in. Bring rope, bring oil, bring more rope. Bjorn went ahead two streets and I haven't heard him since.
note.04: The dead here don't rot right. Same fellow, same spot, three days running. I stopped looking at his face.
note.05: Note to self: when you fall and wake at the stairs again — and you will — do NOT laugh it off. Ask WHY the city won't let you stay dead.
note.06: Carvings everywhere down here. The old scholars called this the Concordance. An engine to 'read the whole world at once.' Madmen.
note.07: Found Rosmund's mark — his sigil, scratched at a junction, pointing down. So the legend was a man after all. He came THIS way.
note.08: An Inquisition patrol turned me back at the cistern. Their captain, Gildar, said: 'Everything you find here wants to finish reading you.' I didn't sleep.
note.09: The fog-folk gave me bread and didn't ask for anything. Their priest, Sando, only smiled and said I'd understand soon. I gave the bread to the rats.
note.10: Rosmund's hand again, firmer: 'The rumor is true and it is a trap. The power is real. The price is everything that wanted it. Do NOT take it as offered.'
note.11: I keep dying and waking at the stairs with all my gear. At first a blessing. Now I count the times. The count is the problem. The count means it has me.
note.12: I finally understand the engine. To rewrite the world you must first BE read — copied in, deleted out. You get your wish and stop being the one who wished it.
note.13: Rosmund again, scrawled, fast: 'Don't be read. Read IT. Edit the engine before it edits you. I think one will can persist. I think. I'm going to try.'
note.14: The Darkness isn't a devil. It's the discards — every draft of every soul the engine ever cut. It only wants to finish the read. A wound wants to close. So does this.
note.15: Sando found me again. 'You fight the fog because you still want things,' he said. 'When you have wanted nothing, you will finally rest.' God help me, it sounded kind.
note.16: Gildar's seal-crew, all dead in a ring, facing outward. They didn't flee. They held the line so the fog wouldn't reach the stairs. I covered their faces.
note.17: Last entry. I've read enough of Rosmund's marks to follow them to the Heart. If you're reading THIS, you're close too. Decide WHO you are before the engine decides for you.
note.18: Rosmund's true hand, the deepest mark: 'It took. I made my edit and I am still I. But I cannot go up — the me that could is gone. I am the only exception, and I am unraveling.'
note.19: If you found my relics, you carry pieces of my will. Two of them, joined, can finish what I started. Free me — or unwrite all of it. Either is mercy. Choose.
note.20: Gildar's final order, sealed in wax: 'Collapse the engine. Seal the city. If I do not return, the wall stays shut forever. The world stays unfinished. That is the gift.'
note.21: Sando left no note. He left a chair, set facing the Heart, and a single line on the floor: 'Sit. Stop wanting. Be complete.'
note.22: (Newest ink, your own future hand?) You will read this and not remember writing it. That alone should tell you how late it is. Go down. End it one way.
inscr.01: TURN BACK. THE SEAL IS MERCY. — by order of the Inquisition
inscr.02: open the eye. let it read you. be finished. — the Open-Eyed
inscr.03: we came to rule the world and the world is reading us back
inscr.04: VEN-OS LE-MOND · OS LE-MOND VEN   (it reads us; we are read)
inscr.05: the engine has no word for 'I'. that is the whole of the danger.
inscr.07: ROSMUND PASSED HERE AND DID NOT TAKE IT. WHY DIDN'T HE TAKE IT.
inscr.08: SOL-VEN OST, MOND-VEN OST   (one will remains, the world remains)
inscr.09: you are not the first you. you are not the last. — scratched a thousand times
muse.band.act1: An abandoned city, forbidden for centuries, and I have it all to myself. Scholarship has never felt so much like grave-robbing.
muse.band.act2: Sigils, on every wall now. Someone built this whole descent to be READ from the bottom up. Down, then. Always down.
muse.band.act3: The corridors don't stay where I leave them. I'm starting to think the city is rewriting itself around me. I'm starting to think I let it.
muse.band.act4: So this is the Heart. It's quiet, the way a held breath is quiet. Whatever I decide here, I decide for everyone.
muse.gold.a: Gold that hums. The old scholars didn't make jewelry — they made arguments, in metal. This one is winning.
muse.gold.b: Rosmund's mark is on it. He didn't lose his treasures down here. He LEFT them. For someone. Maybe for me. That's worse.
muse.lowhp.a: Bleeding, fading — and not afraid. When did I stop being afraid of dying? That's the question that should frighten me.
muse.lowhp.b: If I fall, I'll only wake at the stairs with all my things. A blessing, I used to think. Now I count the wakings.
muse.slaughter.a: Half of these 'monsters' were people once. Adventurers, like me. Half-read, edges torn off. I try not to look at their faces.
muse.slaughter.b: I'm good at this now. Too good. The city is teaching me to be a fixture, one swing at a time.
muse.dark.first: A dark fog, where the city simply... isn't decided yet. The locals call it the Darkness. It isn't hungry for me. It's just unfinished, and so am I.
muse.dark.engulf: It's in my lungs and it doesn't burn — it ERASES. A little less of me each breath. Move. Move while there's still a 'me' to move.
muse.respawn.reveal: Five times now I've died and woken whole. That's not luck. That's a checkpoint. The engine is SAVING me. Which means it's already reading me.
muse.ending.inq: Gildar was right. Some doors should stay shut, even from the inside. Especially from the inside.
muse.ending.cult: Sando was right about one thing: I am so tired of wanting things. The question is whether tired is the same as finished.
muse.ending.self: Limitless power. I came all this way for it. And now I know its only true name: alone, forever, and no longer me.
